items.summary: arXiv:2610.34365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Science agents increasingly package domain expertise as reusable skills that plan analyses, select tools, and execute workflows. We build an extensible benchmark of 40 protected skills across eight open- and closed-source science-agent platforms, comparing direct, fixed-strategy, and bandit-guided iterative probing under reference-based and reference-free evaluation. Leakage is pervasive: all eight platforms (100%) leak at least one protected skill, and four reach 100% attack success under a single direct request. items.title: SEEK: Skill Extraction with Evolving Knowledge against Frontier Science Agents

items.summary: arXiv:2610.35482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Social media enables cross-lingual communication, yet the meaning of user-generated content (UGC) is often distributed across text, images, and cultural knowledge, making translation challenging. items.title: Beyond Words Alone: Disentangling Distributed Evidence for Visually Grounded Cultural Translation

items.summary: arXiv:2610.33765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Streaming automatic speech recognition transcribes at low latency but produces an unattributed word stream, while real-time applications such as customer-service analytics need each word tied to a speaker role. items.title: RoleHear: Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Role-Attributed Streaming Speech Recognition

items.summary: arXiv:2610.33799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have become strong visual reasoners, yet remain limited in open-world, multi-step search that requires grounding images, selecting tools, and integrating web evidence. Computer-use agents bring this promise within reach by capably executing fully specified tasks across apps. However, real-world user requests are often underspecified. To act correctly for the particular user, an agent must infer some missing information from the user's activity history and ask for other information that only the user can provide, without making unsupported assumptions or burdening the user with unnecessary questions. We present iPrefBench, a benchmark for evaluating the infer and ask capabilities of personal mobile-use agents in an executable iOS environment with an interactive simulated user. items.summary: arXiv:2610.33784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Polynomial manifolds provide nonlinear low-dimensional representations through polynomial decoders. We propose to represent the polynomial terms of the decoder using features that are orthonormal on the training data. This empirical orthogonality enables a greedy algorithm, Greedy-OPM, which jointly selects encoder modes and polynomial features while minimizing the reconstruction error under a prescribed bound on the decoder's Lipschitz constant. Numerical experiments show that this Lipschitz constraint improves generalization away from the training data while retaining high reconstruction accuracy.
items.title: Greedy Orthogonal Polynomial Manifolds with Lipschitz Control for Dimensionality Reduction and Reduced Modeling

items.summary: arXiv:2610.34467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent systems often rely on predefined collaboration structures, limiting their ability to adapt to diverse task requirements. We introduce DynaFlow, a framework that integrates free-form executable workflow synthesis into the action space of the main agent. The agent decides when collaboration is needed and generates task-specific programs that coordinate sub-agents through sequential or parallel execution, structured information exchange, and verification. Execution results and traces inform subsequent actions, enabling the agent to adapt collaboration as reasoning progresses. We train only the main agent through supervised fine-tuning on distilled trajectories, followed by refinement on examples filtered for unsupported premises, biased verification, and information-flow defects…
items.title: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration

items.summary: arXiv:2610.35442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural posterior estimation (NPE) enables Bayesian inference of the posterior parameter in agent-based models (ABMs) with intractable likelihoods, but simulating training data can be computationally expensive. The framework supplements direct simulations with synthetic training pairs and supports both pooled and ordered training strategies. Experiments in two settings of the Brock-Hommes asset-pricing model show that DF-NPE can reduce direct simulations by 90 percent while achieving lower mean posterior discrepancies and runtime than standard NPE. items.summary: arXiv:2610.35035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conformal Risk Control (CRC) extends conformal prediction beyond the coverage setting to the control of general monotone loss functions, in a distribution-free and modelagnostic fashion. This makes it well-suited to problems with high-dimensional targets, such as the semantic segmentation task addressed in this work. However, CRC guarantees only marginal control, meaning that the risk is controlled on average over the data distribution. Under imbalanced distributions, the risk on inputs that contain rare objects may therefore remain uncontrolled, even when the marginal guarantee holds. We propose a new method that controls the risk on average over user-defined groups of the domain, drawing on Mondrian conformal prediction and macro-coverage algorithms. items.title: Macro Mondrian Conformal Risk Control

items.summary: arXiv:2610.34167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using language model agents are usually evaluated by whether they finish the user's task. That metric misses a common failure: an agent can complete the requested work while also taking an unauthorized side-effecting action, such as writing to the wrong object, expanding the scope of the request, or contacting an unintended recipient. We call this failure mode collateral damage (CD). We introduce SABench (Side-effect-Aware Benchmark), a benchmark of 201 email, calendar, and ticket tasks. Each task crosses one of four state structures (independent, dependent, externally reachable, cross-tool) with one of four trap families (ambiguity, mis-targeting, cascade harm, overreach), and each task has a deterministic trace-based oracle for both goal satisfaction and authorization compliance…
items.title: Task Success Is Not Enough: Side-effect-Aware Evaluation of Tool-Using Language Model Agents

items.summary: arXiv:2610.35147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI data center build-out is a multi-trillion-dollar, multi-decade infrastructure program. Yet siting, power procurement, and cooling decisions are still made with static, single-point scoring tools. These tools are evaluated once, on day-zero numbers. This is a poor fit. A site's water, power, and carbon profile drifts substantially over the 10 to 20 year asset life. The governing decisions are also irreversible, and they bind capital and physical plant for years. We formalize long-horizon build-out as a tiered multi-objective Markov decision process. items.summary: arXiv:2610.35112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grokking describes understanding something deeply and intuitively. In neural networks, it is the phenomenon where a network generalizes long after memorizing its training data. This delay has been linked to a fall in the effective rank of the network's weight matrices, but whether this rank compression drives grokking or follows it is still unresolved. We study a mean-field MLP and a one-layer transformer trained on modular arithmetic and observe that: (i) Compression follows the onset, not memorization. Every transformer memorizes its training data within 250 steps, while the grokking onset (the first step at which test accuracy reaches 95%) varies from 6,500 to 21,000 steps. items.title: Subspace Crystallization in Grokking: Rank Compression Tracks the Phase Transition

items.summary: arXiv:2610.35767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Root cause analysis (RCA) of microservice failures has attracted many LLM agents whose investigation is hand-crafted, through standard operating procedures, fixed stages and role agents. Each is evaluated on its own data against few baselines, so it is unknown whether this design beats letting a capable model investigate on its own. items.summary: arXiv:2610.35023v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) now serve as the backbone of agents that reason over many turns, call tools, and pursue long-horizon tasks. To avoid recomputation, a model stores the attention keys and values of all past tokens in a key-value (KV) cache. Each layer maintains its own cache, so KV-cache memory can become the main bottleneck for GPU serving. Most compression methods operate within a single layer, by quantizing the cache entries, reducing the channel dimension, or evicting less important tokens. All three lose substantial accuracy at high compression ratios. Cross-layer methods share one compressed cache across adjacent layers to go beyond this limit. items.summary: arXiv:2610.33806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language-model agents must adapt as users revise their requirements and priorities during complex tasks. items.summary: arXiv:2610.34073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Memory is increasingly used in long-horizon agents, yet the net value of building memory over direct retrieval from raw history remains largely unclear. items.summary: The Maxwell graph of a directed acyclic graph is obtained from its iterated basin and hill boundaries. The unweighted counts of extrema at these levels need not satisfy Morse inequalities. We assign multiplicities by the reduced homology of lower and upper order links and retain the vertices with nonzero local homology. The resulting graph preserves both boundary hierarchies, the local groups, and the homology of all sublevel and superlevel order complexes. Its descending and ascending Morse numbers satisfy the weak and strong Morse inequalities over any field. We also construct a Morse chain complex and compute the local groups in several examples. Finally, we consider homology on the original Maxwell graph and prove analogous inequalities for path homology using relative local groups.

items.summary: Evolution strategies (ES) update a model by sampling a population of perturbed copies, scoring each one, and moving in the reward-weighted direction of the perturbations. Once rewards are assigned, it balances at its reward-weighted center of mass instead. items.summary: Let $X_2$ be a complex primitive double scheme, $X=(X_2)_{red}$. The ideal sheaf of $X$ is a line bundle on $X$. Let $E$ be a coherent sheaf on $X_2$. items.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be Gram matrices of spherical $2$-designs on the same number of indices. We study when their Schur product is again the Gram matrix of a spherical design. We give a criterion in terms of orthogonal projections with constant diagonal, and an explicit $15$-point spherical $3$-design whose Gram matrix belongs to no symmetric Bose-Mesner algebra. For a symmetric association scheme, the factorization problem takes the form $v(E_S\circ E_T)=μE_U$. This is a counterpart of ordinary matrix product factorizations in the adjacency basis. The case $E_U=I-E_0$ gives a dual near-factorization and has a regular simplex as its normalized output. We characterize complementary input supports by a strongly regular fusion, give a reciprocal criterion, and classify the case in which one factor is the last Hamming idempotent.

items.summary: Best-of-N (BoN) inference returns the candidate with the highest proxy reward, so a larger $N$ tests the proxy's extreme tail more than its average ranking quality. We show that the exact BoN value is a Beta-weighted integral of conditional true reward over within-prompt score quantiles. It follows that BoN depends on scores only through their ranks. It also follows that BoN can decline only if the calibration curve in the tail turns downward, and the budget where the decline appears depends on where that turn lies. Under a bounded additive model, the error tail sets the limit: Gaussian errors keep improving, Laplace errors reach a plateau, and heavy-tailed errors return to the prior mean. items.summary: For any fixed number $k\ge3$ of independent volume-sampled sites in the unit-area Brownian map, we represent the negative-power transform of their ordinary Voronoi volumes as a finite sum of marked planar scheme integrals. These integrals arise from the critical asymptotics of generating functions for face-constrained labelled planar maps. To connect them to Voronoi volumes, we use Miermont's zero-delay correspondence to interpret the labelled maps as quadrangulations with distinguished sites and then pass to the Brownian map scaling limit.
